questions.title: Who will be appointed Peru's foreign minister in the incoming presidential administration's first cabinet in July 2026?
questions.background: A new presidential administration is scheduled to take office in Peru in July 2026. Its foreign minister will oversee the country's diplomatic relations.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Peruvian government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the person officially appointed minister of foreign affairs in the incoming administration's first cabinet, with the appointment announced by July 31, 2026. Speculation about potential appointments does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed foreign minister's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-23 update incorporating El Comercio's Fernando Vivas July 19 cabinet chronicle and RPP/Andina July 20 transition coverage: Vivas writes that former Sí Creo candidate Carlos Espá is 'so likely to be Foreign Minister that he has rehearsed phrases not to say yes while leaving the clear impression he wants it and believes he will be,' reinforces that Espá's congressional candidate Carla Mares sits on Fujimori's Foreign Ministry transition team (ETTE), and notes designated ministers have pledged silence until inauguration—explaining the lack of official announcements through July 23 while zero competing Canciller names have surfaced 4 days before resolution. Vivas also notes Espá studied at Peru's Diplomatic Academy and worked in the US Embassy press office, fitting Fujimori's pro-US stance and pluripartidario strategy alongside expected Premier Luis Galarreta, while flagging residual veto risk from Torre Tagle's preference for a career diplomat and Espá's sharp anti-China campaign rhetoric. Lifting Carlos Espá 0.45 -> 0.53 (strictly within the <=0.55 unconfirmed-appointment cap), trimming career/former-FM fallbacks Javier González-Olaechea (0.08 -> 0.07; PPC/conservative link noted by Vivas), Hugo de Zela (0.08 -> 0.07), Elmer Schialer (0.05 -> 0.04), and outgoing FM Carlos Pareja (0.04 -> 0.03; met Fujimori July 20 for standard inauguration-dignitaries protocol handover). Top-5 sum = 0.74, preserving 0.26 for another Torre Tagle ambassador or late pluripartidario pick.

questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

questions.title: Which Federal Reserve policymakers will vote for an interest-rate increase at the July 29, 2026 FOMC meeting?
questions.background: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) sets US monetary policy. Its policy announcements disclose members' votes and the policy preferences of dissenting voters.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Federal Reserve's official policy statement and voting record for the meeting concluding July 29, 2026, corroborated by contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution : Identify every voting member whose recorded position favors increasing the federal funds target range relative to the range immediately before the meeting. Include those members whether an increase is adopted or they dissent in favor of one. Accepted Answer Format : All qualifying members' surnames, listed alphabetically and separated by commas.

Consequently, CME FedWatch odds of an actual 25bp rate HIKE on July 29 more than tripled from 11.8% a week ago to 36%-37.9% today (and September hike odds jumped to 83.2%), though the ECB held steady today signaling September. With true July 29 hold probability falling from ~88% to ~65% and hike probability jumping to ~35%: (1) Under a hold (~65%), $100 oil + 187k claims sharply raise the probability that April hawkish dissenter Neel Kashkari rejoins Beth Hammack and Lorie Logan ('Hammack, Kashkari, Logan' 0.10 -> 0.17), while trimming twin dissent 'Hammack, Logan' (0.28 -> 0.21) and slashing solo dissents 'Hammack' (0.15 -> 0.08) and 'Logan' (0.10 -> 0.05) since both already called for hikes pre-blackout when oil was ~$85. (2) Under a Warsh-led majority hike (~35%), all majority voters count under resolution criteria; a unanimous 12-0 hike ('Barr, Bowman, Cook, Hammack, Jefferson, Kashkari, Logan, Paulson, Powell, Waller, Warsh, Williams'—verified 12-voter roster with Powell remaining on Board, Cook retained via June 29 SCOTUS ruling, Warsh succeeding Miran) enters at #4 (0.07, replacing 'Hammack, Logan, Waller' at 0.03), leaving 42% residual across split majority-hike subsets (11-1/10-2/9-3), 3-4 hawk dissents including Waller/Bowman, and a unanimous 12-0 hold.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will announce a finalized voluntary repatriation plan for thousands of Myanmar refugees in August 2026?
questions.background: Repatriation means returning refugees to their country of origin. This question concerns finalization of a government plan, rather than the completion of refugee returns.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government statements or reliable news reporting directly quoting those statements. Resolving Event : During August 2026, a Southeast Asian government publicly confirms that it has finalized a voluntary repatriation programme, or the first phase of such a programme, covering at least 1,000 refugees from Myanmar. A preliminary agreement to consider returns is insufficient. Actual departures need not have occurred. Accepted Answer Format : The common English name of the country finalizing the repatriation plan, not the destination country.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-22 local breaking update (AFP via Straits Times, July 22): Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow confirmed on July 21 that Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing will meet Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok on August 6-7, 2026—directly inside the August 2026 window—following Thailand's July 12 Bangkok ASEAN-Myanmar ministerial talks. Thailand is pursuing an explicit 'dual-track approach' with Naypyidaw on pressing bilateral border issues, already hosts ~80,155 registered Myanmar border-camp refugees under a May-June 2026 camp-closure timeline, and has established UNHCR voluntary-return mechanisms. Conversely, while Malaysia hosts >215,000 UNHCR refugees (>126,000 Rohingya) amid surging domestic anti-Rohingya pressure (July 21 AFP/Straits Times) and engaged Myanmar's FM in May-June, practical Rohingya voluntary repatriation to Arakan Army-contested Rakhine State faces severe barriers (underscored by ~500 Rohingya feared dead in July boat sinkings fleeing Rakhine) and Malaysia has no scheduled August leaders' summit with Min Aung Hlaing. Lifting Thailand 0.52 -> 0.65, trimming Malaysia 0.39 -> 0.28 and Indonesia 0.06 -> 0.04, and keeping Laos (0.01) and Cambodia (0.01) with 1% residual.
